options.a: Medical decision making or total time on the date of the encounter
options.b: History, exam, and MDM, with all three key components required
options.c: Face-to-face time, when counseling exceeds 50 percent of the total visit
options.d: Number of exam bullets documented under the 1997 guidelines

distractorExplanations.c: The 50 percent counseling rule is the pre-2021 time rule; current office E/M uses total time on the date, including non-face-to-face work.
distractorExplanations.b: The three-key-component model was retired for office/outpatient E/M in 2021; history and exam are now only 'medically appropriate'.
distractorExplanations.d: Counting 1997 exam bullets no longer selects office E/M levels; the exam does not drive the level at all since 2021.

distractorExplanations.a: Eighteen months is shorter than the CPT window; a patient seen by the same specialty/group within the past three years is established.
distractorExplanations.c: Five years is not the CPT rule; after three years without a face-to-face service the patient is new again.
distractorExplanations.d: Seven years is a common records-retention figure, not the CPT new-versus-established patient window of three years.

options.a: At least 15 minutes of care for a patient admitted to an intensive care unit
options.b: Moderate-complexity decision making for any patient seen in the ED
options.c: High-complexity decision making for critically ill/injured patients
options.d: High-complexity decision making for a stable patient in an ICU bed

distractorExplanations.a: Location does not define critical care, and 99291 needs at least 30 minutes of critical care time on the date, not 15 minutes.
distractorExplanations.b: Moderate MDM in the ED is an ED E/M service; critical care needs high-complexity care of a critically ill patient.
distractorExplanations.d: A stable patient in an ICU bed is coded with hospital care codes; the ICU location alone is not critical care.

options.a: A patient's own request for a specialist opinion and a written report
options.b: A request for opinion/advice, rendering of services, and a written report
options.c: A request for opinion/advice and the consultant assuming ongoing care
options.d: A provider's request for advice, with a verbal update instead of a written report

distractorExplanations.d: The consultant must send a written report back to the requesting source; a verbal update alone fails the report requirement.
distractorExplanations.a: A patient-initiated request does not qualify; consultations require a request from a physician or other appropriate source.
distractorExplanations.c: Assuming ongoing care is a transfer of care, which is not reported with consultation codes.
